rule: GOAL: Arrange colored blocks to match the target pattern shown at the top of the screen. CONTROLS: Click a block to select it, then click an empty slot to place it there. RULE: Blocks must be placed into the slots in the exact left-to-right order displayed in the goal row. TRAP: Assuming you can place blocks anywhere is wrong; they must go into the specific empty slots in sequence.

GOAL: Place crosses so their arms cover all dots. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the active cross; Space switched active crosses. RULE: Crosses move in fixed steps of three squares per press. TRAP: Assuming dots are collected on contact; they remain until fully covered by an arm.

GOAL: Guide the moving square to the ball by advancing along its trail. CONTROLS: Clicking a dot ahead of the square moves it forward along the diagonal path. RULE: The square always moves a fixed distance toward your click, following the existing trail dots. TRAP: Believing any click moves the square; only clicks on the established trail line advance it correctly.

GOAL: Move the white diamond so the purple midpoint marker lands inside the target ring. CONTROLS: Clicking anywhere moves the white diamond to that exact spot. RULE: The purple marker always sits precisely halfway between the white and gray diamonds. TRAP: Thinking you could click the gray diamond or purple marker to move them directly; only the white diamond responds to input.

GOAL: Move shapes to cover matching dots, absorbing them to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys translate the active shape; Space cycles through shapes. RULE: Shapes must cover all dots of their color, not just touch them. TRAP: Assuming shapes move diagonally or that partial coverage suffices wastes moves.

GOAL: Move the yellow block left to align perfectly with the gap in the black bar. CONTROLS: The bottom blue button shifts the arrow left and adjusts the boundary walls inward. RULE: Each click moves the arrow four units horizontally, so alignment requires precise counting. TRAP: Assuming the arrow moves right when clicking blue; it actually moves left, wasting time if you guess wrong.

GOAL: Grow green and yellow bars until their dots align with matching cross marks. CONTROLS: Click glyphs to adjust bar length; opening direction dictates growth or shrinkage relative to bar orientation. RULE: Glyphs opening toward the bar’s direction shrink it; those opening away expand it. TRAP: Assuming bars complete individually; both must align simultaneously to finish the level.

GOAL: Guide the player from the start room to the exit within the action limit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player between adjacent rooms. RULE: Each move transitions the player to a neighboring room; plan the shortest path to save actions. TRAP: Assuming room coordinates match cell coordinates; remember rooms are spaced two cells apart, so a two-cell gap is a single move.

GOAL: Match all five blue symbols to their pink partners by cycling each column. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor left or right; pressing up or down cycles the current slot. RULE: Blue symbols have fixed pink partners; align each blue hash to its corresponding pink hash. TRAP: Assuming arrows swap symbols directly wastes time; they only select or cycle individual slots.

GOAL: Connect the pipe to both target sockets without touching the bottom bar. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the blue barrier to redirect the flow; Space initiates the test run. RULE: The pipe extends in a straight line until it hits an obstacle, then turns or stops. TRAP: Turning yellow does not mean success; it indicates a wrong path that will trigger a failure.

GOAL: Align the arrow to the marked gap by sliding it right. CONTROLS: Click the lower button to widen the top band and narrow the middle; click the side button to slide the arrow. RULE: The arrow only moves if the middle band has empty space at its edge. TRAP: Believing the arrow moves freely; clicking without first clearing the middle band’s blockage wasted turns.

GOAL: Rotate the ring until the yellow tile aligns with the bracket. CONTROLS: The left arrow rotates the ring counter-clockwise; the right arrow rotates it clockwise. RULE: The yellow bracket marks the fixed target slot for the unique yellow tile. TRAP: Assuming the arrows indicate exit points rather than simple rotation buttons wastes time searching for a non-existent path.

GOAL: Align your shape with the target pattern to unlock the exit. CONTROLS: Arrows move you; picking up items rotates your orientation. RULE: The door only opens when your current rotation matches the required key shape. TRAP: Thinking you could manually rotate without an item wastes time; you must collect the item first.

GOAL: Align the moving charcoal shape with the stationary yellow shape to open the exit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the black player; the charcoal shape moves in the opposite horizontal direction, mirroring the black player’s position. RULE: Horizontal movement is mirrored, so left and right commands reverse for the charcoal target. TRAP: Assuming both shapes move identically wastes time; the charcoal moves opposite to the black player horizontally.

GOAL: Align the plug tips with the terminal cells to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the entire plug assembly in the corresponding direction. RULE: The puzzle solves when the plug tips occupy the same cells as the terminals. TRAP: Assuming tips must touch terminals; they actually need to overlap them completely.

GOAL: Replicate the mini pattern's white cells as red cells on the outer grid. CONTROLS: Clicking an outer grid cell toggles its color between blue and red. RULE: The small preview map indicates exactly which positions must be red to match. TRAP: Assuming the preview was decorative or that blue cells were the target shape.

GOAL: Place all red shapes to fully cover every red dot simultaneously. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected shape; Spacebar switches to the next shape. RULE: Coverage is only checked when all shapes are stationary, requiring exact alignment. TRAP: Assuming dots vanish upon contact; they remain hidden until the level ends, so partial moves do not clear them.

GOAL: Clear the board by reducing all pegs to a single survivor. CONTROLS: Click a peg to select it, then click a valid landing spot to jump. RULE: Jumps must leap directly over an adjacent peg into an empty hole, removing the jumped peg. TRAP: Clicking a landing spot twice cancels the move; click once to jump, then click the new position to select.

GOAL: Match the grid's colors to the two small reference patterns. CONTROLS: Click cells to cycle their colors between blue, red, and orange. RULE: A cell must be red if it corresponds to a white spot in either reference pattern. TRAP: Assuming clicks only toggle between two colors, causing missed steps when cycling through three states.

GOAL: Align the reflection with the target by moving the axis horizontally and toggling vertical movement. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the axis or player; Space transferred energy dots between them, unlocking vertical motion. RULE: The player only moves vertically when holding the energy dots, which Space retrieves from the axis. TRAP: Assuming vertical controls were permanently disabled; they only worked after using Space to activate the player.

GOAL: Move yellow tiles onto matching yellow brackets to complete the puzzle. CONTROLS: Red arrows shifted belts or loops forward; green arrows reversed them. RULE: Tiles matched brackets by color, so yellow tiles fit only yellow slots. TRAP: Assuming belt direction without testing led to wasted moves on unverified arrow behaviors.

GOAL: Navigate to the exit without colliding with the red entity. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one room per press. RULE: The red entity moves one room toward you each turn, but only if you are within two rooms of it. TRAP: Assuming safety in the bottom row; the entity can turn the corner and strike from adjacent diagonal rooms.

GOAL: Flip specific red tiles to orange to form a symmetric diamond pattern. CONTROLS: Click a tile to toggle its color between red and orange. RULE: Each 3x3 mini-grid dictates color changes based on its center tile’s hue. TRAP: Assuming clicks affect neighboring tiles; only the clicked tile changes, so target each cell individually.

GOAL: Rotate the bracket to paint the block’s target side. CONTROLS: Arrows move the bracket between three fixed poses: above, up-left, and left. RULE: The bracket orbits the block in a strict chain; it cannot jump directly across. TRAP: Assuming DOWN works from the top pose; it does nothing until you shift to the side pose first.

GOAL: Drain specific columns to reveal hidden paths. CONTROLS: Click left buttons to raise one column and lower the neighbor. RULE: Water rises to the lower neighbor’s height, never exceeding the container’s top. TRAP: Assuming drained columns vanish; they remain clickable but read as empty, confusing state tracking.

GOAL: Route yellow and orange tokens to their target cells. CONTROLS: Red arrows rotated rings counterclockwise; green arrows rotated them clockwise. RULE: Rings shared corner cells, so moving one ring affected the other at those junctions. TRAP: Assuming rings were independent, ignoring how shared cells transferred tokens between cycles.

GOAL: Rearrange tokens to match target slots using limited moves. CONTROLS: Click one token, then click another to swap their positions. RULE: Swaps exchange locations instantly; no holding or dragging pieces. TRAP: Assuming you can pick up and place a token separately; you must always swap two existing pieces.

GOAL: Match every cell's color to the pattern, turning all blue, orange, or red as required. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell cycles its color from blue to red to orange, then back to blue. RULE: The center cell's color must differ from the base pattern, forcing a shift in the cycle. TRAP: Assuming one click always fixes a cell; orange targets need two clicks, wasting time if you stop early.

GOAL: Place seven lettered tiles into five red and four colored slots to form a complete word sequence. CONTROLS: Click a tray tile to select it, then click a slot to place it; press space to confirm the solution. RULE: Tiles must fit specific color-coded slots, with red tiles filling the top row and others matching their designated bottom colors. TRAP: Assuming tiles could be swapped after placement wastes time; select the correct tile from the tray before placing it to avoid resets.

GOAL: Paint the swatch green by moving the X to the target while keeping the cross orange. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the character; Space switched control between the cross and the X. RULE: Only the active character changes the color of the tile it stands on. TRAP: Believing hidden dots remained visible under the character; they vanish, requiring memory of positions.

GOAL: Arrange letters and a ring to read the exact target sequence. CONTROLS: Click pieces to move them into slots; press space to submit. RULE: The ring inserts the linked box’s contents at its specific position. TRAP: Assuming the ring only connects boxes without altering the linear read order.

GOAL: Align three colored shapes so their protruding tabs lock together into one connected cluster. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected shape; spacebar rotates it; clicking selects a different shape. RULE: Tabs only connect when they perfectly overlap opposing tabs of another shape, turning gray upon contact. TRAP: Assuming you can move shapes through each other; body collisions block movement, requiring precise path planning.

GOAL: Place horizontal bars to block rising water from reaching the top row. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the active bar one block; clicking swaps which bar is active; spacebar starts the water simulation. RULE: Water spreads sideways until it hits a barrier, then rises into the gap above that barrier. TRAP: Thinking water rises immediately; it actually flows horizontally along the surface before finding an opening to ascend.

GOAL: Arrange pieces in two boxes so the red box’s rings point to the blue box, creating a specific nine-item sequence. CONTROLS: Click pieces to move them into slots; press space to check the result. RULE: Each ring in the red box triggers a full read of the blue box, splicing its contents twice into the final list. TRAP: Assuming rings only read once or trying to match the target left-to-right without accounting for the double splice caused confusion.

GOAL: Push the box into the bracket's interior. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active token three spaces; clicks switch which token is active. RULE: Only the token with the white center responds to arrow keys, regardless of distance. TRAP: Assuming the player token is always active wastes time when the box needs independent movement.

GOAL: Fill three colored boxes so a ring chain reads the target sequence exactly. CONTROLS: Click tray items to place them; click boxes to verify; press space to submit. RULE: Each ring jumps to its matching box, reading all slots in order for the final string. TRAP: Placing rings outside the start box breaks the chain, forcing a reset and wasting moves.

GOAL: Move the orange blob to the target ring. CONTROLS: Click handles to select a group, then click positions to move it. RULE: The blob moves to the average position of all its handles. TRAP: Assuming a handle stays active when switching groups wastes clicks on wrong moves.

GOAL: Arrange colored tiles and rings in three nested boxes so reading them produces a specific color sequence. CONTROLS: Click a tray item then a box slot to place it; press Space to verify the arrangement. RULE: A ring inside a box redirects the reading process to the box matching the ring’s color. TRAP: Assuming rings are just markers; they are active instructions that change where the next tile is read from.

GOAL: Lift the strip eight rows to align with the target. CONTROLS: Arrows move the object holding the white dots; Space switches focus between the strip and the shapes. RULE: Only the focused object moves; the white dots mark the active target. TRAP: Assuming arrows always move the strip caused accidental shape displacement when focus was elsewhere.

GOAL: Fill the grid with a checkerboard pattern, matching the hidden mini-hints. CONTROLS: Click plain cells to toggle just that square; click dither cells to toggle themselves plus all four adjacent neighbors. RULE: Dither cells act as cross-switches, forcing you to plan their toggles before fixing isolated mismatches. TRAP: Assuming dither clicks affect diagonals or ignoring their self-toggle leads to endless, confusing correction loops.

GOAL: Move four handles to align the shape's center on the ring. CONTROLS: Click to select a handle; click a target cell to move it. RULE: The center is the average of all handle positions; it must land on an empty ring spot. TRAP: Thinking you must move handles in a fixed order; you can adjust them one by one to shift the center incrementally.

GOAL: Guide the yellow and orange tiles to their matching colored frames. CONTROLS: Arrows slide tiles along horizontal and vertical belts wrapping around the grid. RULE: Tiles move independently along fixed paths, so solve each color’s route separately without blocking the other. TRAP: Assuming tiles block each other or paths intersect; they pass freely, so focus only on reaching targets.

ESTABLISHED: Player moves freely on a six-unit grid. Placing or recalling blocks teleports player to start. Red receiver block remains immovable and unchanged by placement, recall, or proximity. FAILED: Pushing red block down or up. Placing block adjacent to beam. Attempting to pass through red block. Recalling block while adjacent. GOAL IS NOT: Moving the red block. Standing on the block. Blocking the beam with a placed block. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move player. Space places or recalls the carried block.

GOAL: Align the cup and bar to cover yellow zones, then position the mirror strip to reflect them perfectly. CONTROLS: Space switches active object. Arrows move the selected shape or strip. RULE: Reflections flip vertically across the strip; shapes must cover one half, reflections the other. TRAP: Thinking shapes must cover all yellow directly; reflections are required to complete the pattern.

GOAL: Reach the yellow pad to win. CONTROLS: Arrows move the green block; clicking pedestals rotates or swaps nearby shapes. RULE: Red bars are walkable, not walls, allowing direct passage. TRAP: Avoid folding red structures while standing on them to prevent falling or getting stuck.

GOAL: Move the green cluster to the top-left corner. CONTROLS: Click a handle to select it, then click a destination to move it. RULE: The cluster moves as one unit, but its final position depends on the average location of all its handles. TRAP: Assuming you could move the whole group at once; you must reposition individual handles one by one to guide the center.

GOAL: Align all bars over their matching color sources at the bottom. CONTROLS: Click a bar to select it. Arrow keys move it. Space confirms placement. RULE: A bar only locks when fully aligned with its corresponding source column. TRAP: Thinking you could move bars independently; selecting a new bar releases the previous one, so finish each bar’s path before switching.

ESTABLISHED: Arrow keys shift the tip four columns per press, but movement snaps the shape back to 4x4. FAILED: Pressing left at the clamp with a 4x4 tip does nothing; solving the pattern alone does not win. GOAL IS NOT: Simply matching the pattern while holding a full-sized tip at the clamp. CONTROLS: Clicks solve the pattern and shrink the tip to 2x2; arrows move the tip horizontally but force it to expand.

GOAL: Place three distinct boxes into the three wall slots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player and push attached boxes; Space attaches or detaches a box directly in front. RULE: You must face the box to attach it, but detached boxes stay put where dropped. TRAP: Thinking you can attach a box from below; you must stand directly in front of it, facing it.

GOAL: Move the two yellow tiles onto their matching yellow frames. CONTROLS: Click arrows to rotate the main ring or shift the top row of five tiles. RULE: The ring moves all tiles, but the top row shifts independently without affecting the rest. TRAP: Rotating the ring alone cannot align the yellows; you must adjust the top row separately to place them.

GOAL: Clear bricks to widen the ceiling gap so the rising bubble fits. CONTROLS: Arrows move the bubble; clicks break blocks. RULE: The bubble rises only if its full width fits inside the cleared opening. TRAP: Assuming a narrow gap suffices; it does not, requiring multiple blocks removed to widen the path.

ESTABLISHED: The map is a 10x10 grid. Two blue blocks are fixed at coordinates (0,3) and (0,8). FAILED: Attempting to map pixel colors using a 5-pixel stride from the top-left corner failed to align with the logical grid. GOAL IS NOT: A simple pathfinding task between the two blocks. CONTROLS: Pixel sampling requires a specific offset to match logical coordinates; previous coordinate assumptions were incorrect.

ESTABLISHED: Five toggle bars and stems exist; matching patterns do not clear the level. Clicking the ball triggers a plug flicker animation but no victory. FAILED: Matching toggle states to the initial configuration, submitting the ball with aligned toggles, and assuming binary inputs control plug distance. GOAL IS NOT: A simple switch-matching puzzle or a binary code input mechanism. CONTROLS: Clicking toggles flips colors; clicking the ball activates a visual animation without solving the puzzle.

GOAL: Align the horizontal strip to receive the piece. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the selected object; Space cycled selection between the piece, strip, and bar. RULE: Only the object with bright white dots accepts input; blue dots mean it is locked. TRAP: Assuming the piece was active because it looked prominent, when only the strip’s white dots indicated control.

ESTABLISHED: Sockets move up when pushed by the plug. Plug stays in two cells. Wire retracts fully. FAILED: Mouse clicks anywhere. Moving plug without pushing sockets. Trying to force plug into room. GOAL IS NOT: Connecting plug to top sockets. Entering the room. CONTROLS: Arrows move plug and wire. Mouse does nothing. Pushing raises sockets.

GOAL: Paint the bottom triangle orange while keeping the top purple and the middle white. CONTROLS: Arrows rotated your painting angle to cover different grid sections; Space poured ink. RULE: Each angle covered a specific geometric region; only the Southeast angle covered the bottom orange zone. TRAP: Assuming you needed to repaint the white area, when it was already correct and required no action.

GOAL: Shrink the wide tip to a narrow shape and slide it left through the tight channel. CONTROLS: Clicks compress the tip; arrow keys move it horizontally. RULE: The narrow tip fits the left passage, while the wide tip gets stuck. TRAP: Believing arrow keys keep the wide shape causes you to miss the narrow path.

GOAL: Pass the wide tip through a narrow gap to reach the top. CONTROLS: Arrows move the tip; clicking grid cells solves the puzzle. RULE: Solving the pattern shrinks the tip, allowing it to fit through the tight channel. TRAP: Clicking the wrong grid cells wastes moves; only click the white target dots.

GOAL: Slide the hidden X shape to the top dock area. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the shape one grid step per press. RULE: The shape moves in three-pixel jumps, hiding its center under the bottom bar. TRAP: Assuming the visible yellow vertex is the center led to miscounting the required moves.

GOAL: Reach the green exit while surviving red enemies that lunge into their facing cell. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the player one step per press. RULE: Each red enemy faces one direction; entering the cell directly in front of it is instant death. TRAP: Assuming all adjacent cells were safe; you must dodge the specific lunge zone indicated by the enemy’s eye.

GOAL: Shift the block piece to cover the yellow target zone on the left side of the grid. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected piece; spacebar switches between available pieces. RULE: Count empty grid units, not pixels, to calculate the exact number of arrow presses needed. TRAP: Assuming the piece lands on target when yellow dots appear, ignoring that full coverage is required.

ESTABLISHED: The yellow bar is trapped at rows 27-29 and can only move up, preventing it from covering the target area at rows 30-32. FAILED: Attempting to extend bars right or up to reach the target, as walls and arms block all direct paths from current positions. GOAL IS NOT: Simply extending bars to the right or up to cover the cross, as geometry makes this physically impossible with current constraints. CONTROLS: Panel left glyphs shrink bars; right glyphs grow bars; bars move only in their specific growth direction and cannot rotate or jump.

GOAL: Slide the tip into the blob’s target slot. CONTROLS: Arrows push the tip until it hits a wall. RULE: Movement stops only when blocked, not at fixed intervals. TRAP: Assuming small steps wastes time; press firmly for full slides.

GOAL: Align specific glyph shapes into four numbered slots to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys cycle through the available shapes for the currently selected slot. RULE: Only the underlying shape identity matters; any rotation of the correct glyph is accepted. TRAP: Searching for a specific orientation fails when the wheel only holds a rotated version of the target shape.

ESTABLISHED: Two adjacent magenta pieces merged into one purple piece. FAILED: Moving pieces without aligning them; previous attempts to clear the level directly. GOAL IS NOT: Simply placing pieces or keeping magenta pieces separate. CONTROLS: Clicking moves pieces; adjacent same-color pieces merge into the next color in the sequence.

GOAL: Merge two blocks into a single domino shape. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide both blocks simultaneously in the chosen direction. RULE: Blocks occupy distinct cells and cannot pass through each other or overlap. TRAP: Assuming blocks can swap positions by crossing paths, which is impossible here.

GOAL: Guide the green block to the gray tray at the top. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block two spaces; clicking the magenta switch rotates the pink platform. RULE: The block must stand on the platform's pivot point to ride it safely during rotation. TRAP: Believing you can rotate while standing on an arm; this leaves you stranded on the wrong side of the map.

GOAL: Reach the exit without spending the turn limit. CONTROLS: Arrows move you; each move burns one turn. RULE: Turns are finite; running out ends the game immediately. TRAP: Moving back and forth wastes turns, killing you even if safe.

ESTABLISHED: One nub touched the socket arm without winning; pushing it into the terminal broke the socket and failed. FAILED: Connecting only one nub to the socket; breaking the socket structure. GOAL IS NOT: A single connection between the plug and socket; simply touching the socket with one nub. CONTROLS: SPACE rotates the plug around its center; arrow keys translate it.

GOAL: Fill the head's 4x4 interior by growing the tip to a matching 4x4 size. CONTROLS: Arrows move the tip; clicking the diamond pattern toggles its size. RULE: The win condition requires the tip to completely fill the head, not just touch it. TRAP: Assuming a small tip could win by reaching the head wastes moves before realizing it is too small.

ESTABLISHED: The maze is a 5-cell lattice with one box in a bottom-left dead end. The player has visited most reachable spots. FAILED: Moving down into the box from the adjacent cell was blocked. GOAL IS NOT: Pushing the box out of its pocket or entering the box itself. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one cell per press; walls and the box block movement.

GOAL: Reduce the peg count to exactly one. CONTROLS: Click to move the empty hole along the track, then click to jump a peg over another into the empty space. RULE: A peg must jump directly over an adjacent peg to land in the empty hole, removing the jumped peg. TRAP: Assuming the hole moves freely; it only shifts along the specific track, so plan the path carefully before jumping.

ESTABLISHED: Water falls vertically, spreads horizontally along wet surfaces, and drains at the fixed hole. FAILED: Moving bars to block the drain directly fails due to collision. GOAL IS NOT: Simply stopping all water flow; the puzzle likely requires specific placement or timing. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move selected bars; spacebar likely drops or confirms position.

ESTABLISHED: The bubble sits trapped in the bottom-right corner. A vertical channel exists in the upper right, but black barriers at rows 30 and 36 likely block the path from the lower section. FAILED: Clicking distant bricks in the left room did nothing to help the bubble. GOAL IS NOT: Simply clearing the immediate bricks surrounding the bubble, as black gaps remain in the path. CONTROLS: Clicking bricks removes them, but does not clear adjacent black border rows.

GOAL: Guide the electrical spark to push the plug into its matching socket. CONTROLS: Click dark bars to toggle spark gates; click dark stems to block paths. RULE: The spark travels upward through open gates, physically nudging the plug when it collides. TRAP: Believing the plug moves horizontally like a slider; it actually shifts vertically when struck by the rising current.

GOAL: Match yellow row patterns to blue slots using rotation orbits. CONTROLS: UP/DOWN rotate the current slot’s glyph wheel; RIGHT moves the cursor to the next slot. RULE: A blue glyph fits a yellow slot only if their rotation orbits are identical, regardless of starting angle. TRAP: Assuming pairs were defined by horizontal proximity rather than distinct row-half groupings led to incorrect signal mapping.

ESTABLISHED: The vertical arrow (6x6) is too wide for the 3-wide gray slot. FAILED: Attempting to push the vertical arrow through the narrow vertical slot. GOAL IS NOT: Forcing the vertical arrow through the slot or rotating it. CONTROLS: Mouse drags objects; no rotation or resizing controls exist.

GOAL: Place three yellow stars into the bottom row of the central frame. CONTROLS: Rotate individual star clusters to move pieces; click the center to swap top and bottom rows. RULE: The central swap is reversible, letting you stage pieces on top before dropping them down. TRAP: Trying to place all pieces at once fails; you must stage them on the top row first.

ESTABLISHED: Blob2 is currently white and must absorb colors from static paint patches to match the ring. FAILED: Attempting to solve by guessing handle coordinates without verifying paint transfer mechanics. GOAL IS NOT: Simply placing any blob on the ring; the blob must acquire specific colors first. CONTROLS: Moving the blob's center over a static patch transfers its colors to the blob's halves.

GOAL: Reach the green block before patrolling oranges capture it. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player; every valid step advances the game clock. RULE: Oranges move two rooms per player turn in fixed, predictable cycles. TRAP: Assuming a blocked move pauses the clock; it is a wasted turn where enemies still advance.

GOAL: Translate sky row glyphs through pink to yellow row to match pair types. CONTROLS: Arrows move cursor and cycle yellow glyph choices. RULE: Sky maps to pink, then yellow, via matching pair instances. TRAP: Assuming all pair instances are identical; they are not, requiring precise glyph matching.

GOAL: Shift the bottom-right tile to the top-right corner. CONTROLS: Green buttons rotate the inner block; red buttons shift the outer frame. RULE: Block rotations and frame shifts are independent moves that can be combined. TRAP: Assuming the two yellow tiles interact or block each other, when they operate in separate zones.

ESTROLISHED: Five masks are fixed. The target is unreachable with current mechanics. The top region matches the bottle's ink shape perfectly. FAILED: Clicking the block center. Pouring from standard poses. Assuming ink depletion occurs. GOAL IS NOT: Solvable with current five masks alone. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the bracket. Space pours ink. Mouse clicks on the bottle ink may trigger a top-center pour.

ESTABLISHED: The bar's interior is blocked. A safe detour around the bar exists, costing thirteen moves to reach the bottom-right slot. FAILED: Attempting to cross the bar directly from the starting position. GOAL IS NOT: Placing boxes inside the bar structure. CONTROLS: Directional keys move the player and push adjacent boxes. Space places a held box.

ESTABLISHED: The charcoal shape matches the first piece mirrored horizontally and shifted upward, not rotated or moved normally. FAILED: Treating the piece as a standard rigid body; assuming simple translation; trying vertical flips; assuming the mirror axis is the strip itself. GOAL IS NOT: A simple rotation puzzle; a standard sliding block challenge; a test of spatial memory alone. CONTROLS: Movement triggers a complex reflection and translation based on hidden axes, not direct placement.

ESTABLISHED: Tokens move three cells per press. Purple structures block movement. FAILED: Pressing UP on the bottom-left token did nothing. GOAL IS NOT: Fitting tokens into holes within their starting rooms. CONTROLS: Directional keys move tokens three cells until they hit a wall or obstacle.

GOAL: Paint the canvas by filling regions with specific colors. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate the pourer, Space pours the selected color, Clicks select colors or bottles. RULE: Pour order determines layering; later pours overwrite earlier ones in overlapping areas. TRAP: Assuming all regions can be painted independently; overlapping zones require precise sequencing to avoid unwanted coverage.

GOAL: Match top word tiles to bottom sentence chunks using a seven-entry glyph wheel. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor between tiles; UP cycles the current tile’s glyph. RULE: The cursor visits only the eight top word tiles, skipping the bottom rows entirely. TRAP: Assuming UP rotates the glyph locally instead of cycling it through the full dictionary wheel.

ESTABLISHED: The green block moves two cells per step but is blocked by purple fence and charcoal cells. FAILED: Moving green right toward the yellow pad is blocked; rotating the red pedestal twice returns it to horizontal. GOAL IS NOT: Reaching the yellow pad with the green block. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the green block two cells; clicking the red pedestal rotates it 90 degrees.

ESTABLISHED: The pair is currently at column 5, rows 10 and 11. The win condition requires them to be vertically adjacent within the gap at column 6. FAILED: Pressing RIGHT while adjacent causes the pair to split apart, moving them away from the target instead of completing the level. GOAL IS NOT: Simply being adjacent to each other anywhere on the grid is insufficient; they must specifically occupy the gap cells. CONTROLS: LEFT shifts the left block left and the right block right; RIGHT shifts the left block right and the right block left.

ESTABLISHED: The square's top edge acts as a barrier, hiding the player and blocking downward movement into the interior. FAILED: Repeated downward presses from the top edge result in no movement, leaving the player stuck on the boundary. GOAL IS NOT: Simply pushing the square or entering its interior from the top. CONTROLS: Down moves the player until hitting the square's edge, where it becomes ineffective.

ESTABLISHED: The room sits at a specific rail junction. A long black corridor extends to the right. Several empty slots exist in distant blocks, some partially blocked by pegs. The grid follows a strict six-unit spacing pattern. FAILED: Blindly counting empty slots as valid destinations. Assuming all black lines are open paths. Ignoring the specific alignment of pegs within the distant blocks. GOAL IS NOT: Simply filling every visible hole. The room does not need to visit every block. Not all empty spaces are reachable or relevant. CONTROLS: Direction keys move the room along black rails. The

GOAL: Slide the yellow block onto the target marker. CONTROLS: Click to push blocks in a direction. RULE: Blocks slide until they hit a wall or another block. TRAP: Thinking clicks move blocks one step; they glide fully across the board.

GOAL: Cover the gap with both pieces. CONTROLS: Arrows move pieces; SPACE acts separately. RULE: Victory checks only after arrow moves, not SPACE. TRAP: Pressing SPACE while merged in the gap failed to trigger a win.

ESTABLISHED: Bar1, Bar2, and Stem2 do nothing. Stem1 scales the piece twice. Pair0 moves the piece left. The animation reveals every intermediate position. FAILED: Using bar1, bar2, or stem2. Assuming the right bank contains an UP command. Treating the left half as active without testing the cartridge box.
